effect: The tendon cells used amino acids to build collagen fibres outside themselves, completing the chapter. That contrasted with the muscle cells' pulling proteins inside the cells.
reaction: The comparison made the different jobs of the two cell groups clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the muscle cells was most worthwhile: the picture connected RNA instructions to fibres that can slide and shorten a cell.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two signal-to-RNA sequences felt somewhat repetitive, although comparing their different results helped.

surprise.text: I was surprised that muscle cells keep their pulling proteins inside while tendon cells build fibres outside, despite retaining the same DNA set.

arbitrary.text: The signal pairings were clear from the pictures and goals, but why Sonic hedgehog and TGF-beta2 produce those specific effects was not explained in detail. I followed the named pairings rather than understanding the mechanism.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing how the different protein structures support muscle and tendon jobs makes me curious about how the larger parts are assembled.
